title: Take a burger patty's temperature through its side: hold it with a turner, probe level to the centre
instruction: Take the burger patty's temperature: hold it still with the turner, push the thermometer's probe in level through the side of the patty until its tip is at the centre, hold it still for the reading, then draw it out and lay the thermometer and the turner back down.
context: Checking that meat is cooked through is core work for the 1.4 million US restaurant cooks (O*NET 35-2014: "Observe and test foods to determine if they have been cooked sufficiently"; ground beef must reach 160 F). For a burger the USDA's food-safety agency says: "When cooking hamburger patties ... insert the food thermometer through the side. Make sure the food thermometer reaches the center." Its fact sheet warns that "the reading will only be correct ... if the thermometer is placed in the proper location in the food". The patty is 23 mm thick: the tip must end 50 mm in, inside a band under 8 mm tall, so a probe tilted by more than about 4 degrees misses it and by more than about 13 comes out of the top or bottom face, and the push slides a patty nobody holds. So one hand holds it down with the turner while the other drives the probe in level and holds it still for the 1-second reading, hands about 34 cm apart.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. (1) A white co-polymer cutting board, San Jamar CB121812WH, 457 x 305 x 12.7, held still (on a damp cloth), long side along y from y -50 to 407, centred on x 300. (2) A cooked 8 oz (227 g raw) 80/20 beef burger patty, 100 across and 23 thick with a rounded edge, 170 g, browned top and bottom, lying flat on the board, centre at x 300, y 30 (its right edge 30 from the board's right edge). (3) A Dexter-Russell Sani-Safe Cool Blue 19713H hamburger turner, 140 g: solid stainless blade 102 x 76 x 1.2 with bevelled edges, handle raised 28 by the offset, blue handle 127 x 24 x 18; lying on its blade on the board along y, centred on x 300, the blade's front edge at y 95 (15 left of the patty), handle toward the left arm. (4) A ThermoWorks Thermapen ONE instant-read thermometer, 115 g, red body 156 x 48 x 19, its 110 mm steel probe (3.3 thick, narrowing to 1.5 over the last 12) folded out straight; lying display up on the bench right of the board, body centre at x 215, y -262, probe pointing left at the patty, along y, 17 off the body's centre line toward x+, its tip at y -74. Real trials: tape marks at these positions. Real patty: one from a batch made as the reset notes say (8 oz 80/20 beef pressed in a 114 (4.5 in) ring, browned, cooked and held in a 160 F water bath), 100 +/- 5 across and 23 +/- 2 thick, 160 F through at the start.
scoring: Judged over the whole trial from where the probe's tip goes inside the patty. Side entry: the probe goes in through the patty's edge, not its top or bottom face, within 20 degrees of level. Centre: the tip within 12 mm of the patty's centre line and within 3.8 mm of its mid-height (the middle third). Breakout: the tip comes out through the top or bottom face. 1.0: a reading taken (the tip at the centre in a side entry without breakout, the patty moved under 15 mm, the tip still, under 5 mm/s, for at least 1 s, the Thermapen ONE's response time), then the probe drawn out, the thermometer lying flat on the bench off the board, the turner lying flat on its blade, both let go (grippers 3 cm clear of thermometer, turner and patty), the patty moved under 15 mm from its start and not flipped, everything still for 1 s. 0.75: the reading taken, but not all put down. 0.5: the tip reached the centre in a side entry without breakout, the patty moved under 15 mm. 0.25: a side entry. 0: no side entry (a probe pushed in through the top face never counts), or the patty flipped or off the board. Real trial: the probe's depth is 110 mm minus the length still showing (ruler); its height and angle from a side photo; after withdrawal the hole in the edge (ruler) and no exit hole on the top or bottom; tape marks round the patty; the reading held steady on the display for 1 s.
reset_notes: One patty is used up per trial (a probed one has a hole); wipe the probe; lay the thermometer and the turner back at their marks. Batch, made on the trial day: weigh 227 +/- 2 g (8 oz) portions of cold 80/20 ground beef; press each in a 114 mm (4.5 in) ring into an even round patty; sear each side in a very hot skillet until browned (about 1 min a side, an estimate); seal each flat in its own zip-top bag and cook them in a sous-vide water bath at 160 F (71 C) for at least 1 h (an estimate). They stay in the bath until used, held at 160 F (above the USDA's 140 F minimum for hot food), so each starts its trial at 160 +/- 3 F through. Make one more than the trials, the witness: before the first trial probe it through the side (it must read 160 +/- 3 F) and weigh it (record it: the modelled 170 g is an estimate); then throw it away. Each patty, checked with a ruler as it is placed: 100 +/- 5 mm across both ways, 23 +/- 2 mm thick at its edge, lying flat; one outside these is thrown away and the next used (if several fail, change the ring for the next batch). Handling: keep the raw beef at 40 F or below until it is portioned, and no more than 2 h out of refrigeration before it goes into the bath (USDA); wash hands and tools after raw meat; move cooked patties with tongs. No patty is eaten: probed patties, and any left at the session's end, are thrown away. Between trials, about 3 minutes: lift the probed patty into the waste bin and wipe the board dry; take the next bag from the bath, open it and slide the patty onto its tape marks (a 100 mm circle round its centre mark), blot it dry and check it with the ruler; wipe the probe; lay the thermometer and the turner at their marks; start the trial within 2 minutes of taking the patty from the bath.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies, 20 Hz. The patty is rigid with no hole: when the probe's tip crosses its surface the task file joins probe and patty by a D6 joint along the probe's own line there. Along it, 1 N of cutting plus 0.015 N per mm of shaft in the meat resists both ways; across it, stiffness and a 0.05 N/mm tearing limit grow with depth, so the meat steers the probe and a tilted entry runs to a face. All estimates. No squash, juices, crumbs or heat; the reading is the tip's place. Board fixed.
